records.source: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Like for is the kingdom of the heavens to a man a master of a house, who went out in [the] morning to hire workmen for the vineyard of him.
pieces: For this is what the kingdom of heaven is like: a landowner went out at first light to hire laborers to work in his vineyard.

L.1: For the kingdom of the heavens is like a man, a master of a house, who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

R.1: The kingdom of heaven is like this. A man owned a vineyard, a field of grapevines. Early one morning he went out to find workers and hire them to work in it.

decisions.choice: for: the story explains the saying just before it
alternatives: a new start with no link
decisions.reason: The story opens with "for" and illustrates the saying about the first and the last (19:30). The same saying, with its halves turned around, closes it (20:16). Jesus is still answering Peter (19:27).

decisions.choice: a master of a house: the head of a household who owned land
decisions.reason: The word means the master of a household, here a man who owned a vineyard and hired day laborers (as in 13:27 and 21:33).

decisions.choice: early in the morning: at daybreak, when laborers waited to be hired
decisions.reason: Day laborers gathered in the marketplace at sunrise, hoping to be hired for the day. The work went on until evening (20:8).

decisions.choice: is like: the kingdom is like the whole story, not the man alone
alternatives: the kingdom is like a landowner
decisions.reason: As in 13:24 and 13:45, the comparison is with what happens in the story, not with its first character.

decisions.choice: landowner (B); a man owned a vineyard (R)
decisions.reason: The man is the owner of the estate, not only of a house, so Balanced and Readable say what he owned. The landowner is a figure in a story, so his pronouns take no deity_pronoun span, though the story is about God.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer to Peter, begun in 19:28, runs on into the story, so the quotation left open at 19:30 continues here and closes at 20:16.

decisions.choice: a vineyard, a field of grapevines
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a vineyard is.

records.heading: Workers hired at every hour

records.source: συμφωνήσας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Having agreed then with the workmen for a denarius the day he sent them into the vineyard of him.
pieces: He settled with the laborers on {{units:the usual wage for a day|a denarius for the day}} and sent them off into his vineyard.

L.2: And having agreed with the workers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.

R.2: He agreed to pay them {{units:the normal pay for one day's work|a denarius for the day}}. Then he sent them into his vineyard.

decisions.choice: a denarius for the day: a fair, ordinary day's wage
decisions.reason: A denarius was a Roman silver coin. It was the usual pay for a laborer's day of work, enough to feed a family for a day. The workers agree to a fair wage.

decisions.choice: having agreed: a spoken contract made before the work
decisions.reason: The first workers have a fixed agreement. The owner later reminds them of it (20:13).

decisions.choice: {{units:the usual wage for a day|a denarius for the day}}
alternatives: a denarius for the day only
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the coin's worth by default, with the original coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the denarius.

records.source: καὶ ἐξελθὼν περὶ τρίτην ὥραν εἶδεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἀργούς·
records.gloss: And having gone out about [the] third hour he saw others standing in the marketplace idle;
pieces: Around nine in the morning he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace with nothing to do.

L.3: And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace,

R.3: At about nine o'clock in the morning, he went out again. He saw some other people standing around in the marketplace. No one had given them work.

decisions.choice: about the third hour: about nine in the morning
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise in twelve hours (John 11:9), so the third hour was about nine in the morning.

decisions.choice: idle: without work, not lazy
decisions.reason: The word means not working. The men at the eleventh hour explain that no one has hired them (20:7).

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the town square where laborers waited to be hired
decisions.reason: The open square of a town was where people traded and where workers waited for an employer.

decisions.choice: nine in the morning (B); nine o'clock in the morning (R)
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

decisions.choice: No one had given them work.
decisions.reason: Readable says why they were idle, as 20:7 explains, and adds "again" since he had gone out once already.

records.source: καὶ ἐκείνοις εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾖ δίκαιον δώσω ὑμῖν·
records.gloss: and to them he said, Go also you into the vineyard, and whatever might be right I will give you;
pieces: 'You too, go to the vineyard,' he told them, 'and I will give you what is fair.'

L.4: and to them he said, 'You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.'

R.4: He said to them, 'You can go and work in my vineyard too. I will pay you what is fair.'

decisions.choice: whatever is right: a fair wage, not a set sum
alternatives: the righteous thing in God's sight
decisions.reason: The owner names no sum. The workers trust him to pay what is fair.

decisions.choice: go and work in my vineyard
decisions.reason: Readable says why they go.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside the story
decisions.reason: The whole story is told by Jesus, so the words of the people in it are a quotation inside his speech.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον.
records.gloss: And they went.
pieces: So they went.

decisions.choice: they went: they took the work without a set wage
decisions.reason: They went into the vineyard on the owner's word alone.

records.source: πάλιν ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως.
records.gloss: Again having gone out about [the] sixth and ninth hour he did likewise.
pieces: He went out again around noon, and again around three in the afternoon, and did the same.

L.5: Again, going out about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did likewise.

R.5: He went out again at about twelve noon and at about three in the afternoon. Each time he did the same thing.

decisions.choice: the sixth and ninth hour: about noon and about three in the afternoon
decisions.reason: Counting from sunrise, the sixth hour was midday and the ninth was the middle of the afternoon.

decisions.choice: likewise: he hired more workers on the same terms
decisions.reason: He did as at the third hour, sending them in with a promise of what is fair.

decisions.choice: noon; three in the afternoon
alternatives: the sixth and the ninth hour
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

records.source: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί;
records.gloss: About then the eleventh having gone out he found others standing, and he says to them, Why here have you stood all the day idle?
pieces: Then, about five in the afternoon, he went out and found still others standing there. 'Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?' he asked them.

L.6: And going out about the eleventh [hour], he found others standing, and he says to them, 'Why have you been standing here idle the whole day?'

R.6: At about five o'clock in the afternoon, he went out again and found more people standing there. He asked them, 'Why have you been standing here all day without working?'

decisions.choice: the eleventh hour: about five in the afternoon, one hour before work ended
decisions.reason: The eleventh hour was about an hour before sunset. The other workers say these men worked only one hour (20:12).

decisions.choice: the eleventh, without "hour"; standing, without "idle"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "hour" after "the eleventh" and "idle" after "standing", which say the same thing more fully. The SBLGNT follows earlier manuscripts that lack both. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: five in the afternoon (B); five o'clock in the afternoon (R)
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο.
records.gloss: They say to him, Because no one us has hired.
pieces: 'Because nobody has hired us,' they answered.

L.7: They say to him, 'Because no one has hired us.'

R.7: They answered, 'No one has hired us.'

decisions.choice: because no one has hired us: they wanted work but found none
decisions.reason: Their answer explains why they are idle. The owner takes them at their word.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα.
records.gloss: He says to them, Go also you into the vineyard.
pieces: He told them, 'You go to the vineyard too.'

L.7: He says to them, 'You also go into the vineyard.'

R.7: He told them, 'Then you can go and work in my vineyard too.'

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends with the vineyard; no wage is promised
alternatives: adds: and whatever is right you will receive
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and whatever is right you will receive", repeating 20:4. Earlier manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: go and work in my vineyard
decisions.reason: As in 20:4, Readable says why they go.

records.source: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ· Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος αὐτοῖς τὸν μισθὸν ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων.
records.gloss: Evening then having come says the master of the vineyard to the foreman of him, Call the workmen and pay them the wages, having begun from the last unto the first.
pieces: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard told his manager, 'Call in the laborers and give them their pay. Start with the ones hired last and finish with the first.'

L.8: And when evening had come, the master of the vineyard says to his foreman, 'Call the workers and pay them the wages, beginning from the last up to the first.'

R.8: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard spoke to the man in charge of his workers. He said, 'Call the workers and pay them. Begin with the people I hired last, and end with the ones I hired first.'

decisions.choice: evening: the end of the working day, when wages were paid
decisions.reason: The law told employers to pay a hired worker before sunset on the day of the work (Leviticus 19:13; Deuteronomy 24:14-15).

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the vineyard
decisions.reason: The word can mean "lord". In the story it is the owner, though the story points to God.

decisions.choice: foreman: a manager put in charge of the estate's business
decisions.reason: The word is used of a steward or manager who acted for the owner.

decisions.choice: from the last to the first: the order lets the first see what the last receive
decisions.reason: Because the last are paid first, those hired first see their pay and expect more (20:10). The order also acts out the saying in 20:16.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: owner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word that says who he is in the story.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον.
records.gloss: And having come those about the eleventh hour they received each a denarius.
pieces: Those hired around five o'clock came, and each of them was given {{units:a full day's wage|a denarius}}.

L.9: And those [hired] about the eleventh hour came, and they received a denarius each.

R.9: The workers who started at five o'clock came first. Each of them got {{units:a full day's pay|a denarius}}.

decisions.choice: a denarius each: a whole day's wage for one hour's work
decisions.reason: The last workers receive what the first agreed to for a full day. This is the surprise of the story.

decisions.choice: {{units:a full day's wage|a denarius}}
decisions.reason: As in 20:2, the coin's worth is the default and the coin itself the alternative.

decisions.choice: five o'clock
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι πλεῖον λήμψονται· καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί.
records.gloss: And having come the first thought that more they will receive; and they received each a denarius also themselves.
pieces: So when the first ones came, they expected to get more. But they too were each paid {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}}.

L.10: And when the first came, they thought that they would receive more; and they themselves also received a denarius each.

R.10: Then the workers who had been hired first came. They thought they would get more money. But each of them also got {{units:one day's pay|a denarius}}.

decisions.choice: they also: the same pay as the last, and what they had agreed to
decisions.reason: They receive exactly the wage they agreed to in 20:2. What troubles them is that the last receive it too.

decisions.choice: {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}}
decisions.reason: As in 20:2.

records.source: λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου λέγοντες· Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἴσους αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα.
records.gloss: Having received now they were grumbling against the master of the house \v 12 saying, These the last one hour worked, and equal them to us you have made, those having borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.
pieces: When they were paid, they began to grumble at the landowner.
'The ones who came last put in a single hour,' they said, 'and you have treated them the same as us, though we carried the load of the whole day in the burning heat.'

L.11: And having received [it], they were grumbling against the master of the house,
L.12: saying, 'These last ones worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.'

R.11: When they got their pay, they started to complain about the owner.
R.12: They said, 'These people who came last worked for only one hour. But you paid them the same as us! We worked hard all day long in the hot sun.'

decisions.choice: were grumbling: kept muttering complaints
decisions.reason: The verb pictures low, resentful complaint, and the tense shows that it went on. Israel grumbled against God in the wilderness in the same way (Exodus 16:7-8).

decisions.choice: you have made them equal to us: the complaint is equal treatment
decisions.reason: They do not say they were paid less than agreed. They object that the others were treated as their equals.

decisions.choice: the scorching heat: the burning heat of the day, perhaps the hot east wind
decisions.reason: The word is used of burning heat and of the hot wind from the desert (Jonah 4:8; James 1:11).

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" to give the tone of the complaint, which the Greek gives by setting one hour against the whole day.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἑταῖρε, οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε· οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι;
records.gloss: And answering to one of them he said, Friend, not I do wrong you; not for a denarius did you agree with me?
pieces: But he replied to one of them, 'Friend, I have done you no wrong. Was it not for {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}} that you made your agreement with me?

L.13: But he answered one of them and said, 'Friend, I am not doing you wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?

R.13: The owner answered one of them, 'Friend, I am not cheating you. You agreed to work for {{units:one day's pay|a denarius}}, did you not?

decisions.choice: Friend: a polite address to someone who is in the wrong
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word only when the one spoken to is at fault (22:12; 26:50). It is courteous but cool.

decisions.choice: I am not doing you wrong: I am not being unjust to you
decisions.reason: The owner kept the agreement exactly. Fairness is not the question; generosity is (20:15).

decisions.choice: {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}}
decisions.reason: As in 20:2.

decisions.choice: the owner's words run on to 20:15
decisions.reason: The owner's answer runs through three sentences, so the inner quotation opens here and closes at the end of 20:15.

records.source: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε· θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί·
records.gloss: Take what [is] yours and go; I desire now to this the last to give as also to you;
pieces: Take what is yours and be on your way. It is my choice to give this last worker just what I gave you.

L.14: Take what [is] yours and go. But I want to give to this last [one] as also to you.

R.14: Take your money and go home. I have decided to pay the worker who came last the same as you.

decisions.choice: I want: it is my will, my free choice
decisions.reason: The owner's wish is the reason for the gift. He takes nothing from anyone by giving it.

decisions.choice: go: a dismissal
decisions.reason: The working day is over, and the owner sends him away with his pay.

records.source: οὐκ ἔξεστίν μοι ὃ θέλω ποιῆσαι ἐν τοῖς ἐμοῖς;
records.gloss: Not is it lawful for me what I will to do with that which [is] mine?
pieces: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what belongs to me?

L.15: Is it not lawful for me to do what I want with what [is] mine?

R.15: I have the right to do what I want with my own money.

decisions.choice: lawful: permitted, within my rights
alternatives: required by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word is used of what is allowed. The money is the owner's, and no rule forbids him to give it.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Is it not lawful for me ...?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: my own money
decisions.reason: Readable names what the owner's own things are in the story.

records.source: ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι;
records.gloss: Or the eye of you evil is because I good am?
pieces: Or do you look on my generosity with an evil eye?'

L.15: Or is your eye evil because I am good?'

R.15: Or are you angry and jealous that I am kind to others?'

decisions.choice: an evil eye: envy, a grudging spirit
decisions.reason: In Hebrew an "evil eye" means a grudging, envious attitude (Deuteronomy 15:9; Proverbs 28:22). Jesus uses the same phrase in 6:23. Here it is the look of someone who resents another person's good fortune.

decisions.choice: good: generous, kind
decisions.reason: The word means good, and here it is the goodness of a generous giver. The play is between the worker's evil eye and the owner's good heart.

decisions.choice: do you look on my generosity with an evil eye
alternatives: are you envious because I am generous
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the evil eye, as in 6:23, and joins it to what the man looks on.

decisions.choice: angry and jealous
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: οὕτως ἔσονται οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι.
records.gloss: Thus will be the last first and the first last.
pieces: That is how it will be: those who are last will be first, and those who are first, last."

L.16: Thus the last will be first, and the first last."

R.16: So people who are last now will be first then. And people who are first now will be last."

decisions.choice: the last first: God's reward is a gift, given as he chooses
alternatives: a warning that the first will be shut out
decisions.reason: The saying repeats 19:30 in reverse order and frames the story. Those who came late receive the same as those who worked all day; no one can claim a higher place by work done.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends with "the first last"
alternatives: adds: for many are called, but few are chosen
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "For many are called, but few are chosen", which appears to come from 22:14. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: now ... then
decisions.reason: Readable says when the change comes: now, and in the kingdom.

decisions.choice: the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer to Peter, begun in 19:28 and continued through the story, ends here.

records.source: Καὶ ἀναβαίνων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν, καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·
records.gloss: And going up Jesus to Jerusalem he took the twelve disciples aside by themselves, and on the way he said to them:
pieces: As Jesus was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way up to Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the twelve disciples aside, away from the others, and spoke to them as they walked.

L.17: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the twelve disciples aside by themselves, and on the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,

R.17: Jesus was going up to Jerusalem. On the way, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers to a place away from the other people. He said to them,

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: the city stood high in the hills
decisions.reason: Jerusalem lies high in the hill country, and travelers always spoke of going up to it. Jesus is now on the road from the Jordan valley (19:1; 20:29).

decisions.choice: aside by themselves: away from the crowds traveling with them
decisions.reason: Large crowds were following him (19:2; 20:29). This teaching is for the Twelve alone.

decisions.choice: the twelve disciples
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "disciples" and read "the Twelve". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what disciples are, as in 5:1.

records.heading: A third warning of death and rising

records.source: Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ, καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται.
records.gloss: Behold we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death \v 19 and they will hand over him to the Gentiles to mock and to flog and to crucify, and on the third day he will be raised.
pieces: "We are going up to Jerusalem now. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will sentence {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death

and turn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles, who will mock {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whip {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised to life."

L.18: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death
L.19: and will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles to mock and to flog and to crucify, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised."

R.18: "Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the leading priests and the teachers of the law. They will decide that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die.
R.19: Then they will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to people who are not Jews. Those people will make fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with whips, and nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross to die. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised from death."

decisions.choice: handed over: given into the power of others
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Judas betraying Jesus (10:4; 26:15) and of the leaders handing him to Pilate (27:2) and Pilate handing him to be crucified (27:26). The passive in 20:18 leaves open who hands him over, and in the end God's plan stands behind it (26:24).

decisions.choice: mock, flog, crucify: the Roman way of executing slaves and rebels
decisions.reason: This is the first time in Matthew that Jesus names crucifixion as the way he will die (compare 16:21; 17:22-23). Crucifixion was a Roman punishment, often after a flogging, as happened to Jesus (27:26-31).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the Roman authorities
decisions.reason: Judea was under a Roman governor, and the Jewish council could not carry out an execution on its own (John 18:31). The leaders hand Jesus to Pilate (27:2).

decisions.choice: will be raised: God will raise him
alternatives: he will rise by his own power only
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, as in 16:21 and 17:23, and points to God as the one who raises him. It can also be read as "will rise".

decisions.choice: look (L); "now" (B); "Listen!" (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain names used in 2:4.

decisions.choice: nail him to a cross to die
decisions.reason: Readable says what crucifying is.

records.source: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι παρ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Then came to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee with the sons of her kneeling down and asking something from him.
pieces: Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} together with her sons. She knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a favor.

L.20: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with her sons, kneeling down and asking something from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.20: Then the mother of James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus with her sons. She bowed down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to do something for her.

decisions.choice: the mother of the sons of Zebedee: the mother of James and John
decisions.reason: Zebedee's sons are James and John (4:21; 10:2). Their mother is with the women at the cross (27:56). Mark 10:35 has the brothers make the request themselves; in Matthew their mother speaks for them, and Jesus answers the sons (20:22).

decisions.choice: kneeling down: bowing low in honor, as before a king
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down before someone in honor. The magi did it before the child king (2:11). Her request is about his kingdom.

decisions.choice: James and John
decisions.reason: Readable names the sons, as 4:21 and 10:2 do.

records.heading: A mother's request for her sons

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Τί θέλεις;
records.gloss: And he said to her, What do you desire?
pieces: "What is it you want?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked her.

L.21: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "What do you want?"

R.21: Jesus asked her, "What do you want?"

decisions.choice: what do you want: an invitation to name the request
decisions.reason: Jesus asks her to say what she wants, as he asks the blind men in 20:32.

records.source: λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν σου καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.
records.gloss: She says to him, Say that might sit these the two sons of me one on [the] right of you and one on [the] left of you in the kingdom of you.
pieces: She said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word that in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom these two sons of mine will sit beside {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left."

L.21: She says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom."

R.21: She said, "Promise me that my two sons will sit next to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule as king. Let one sit at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side and the other at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left side."

decisions.choice: at your right and left: the places of highest honor beside a king
decisions.reason: The seat at a king's right hand was the place of greatest honor (1 Kings 2:19; Psalm 110:1). Jesus had just spoken of the Twelve sitting on thrones (19:28).

decisions.choice: say: give the word, decree it
decisions.reason: She asks Jesus to declare it as a king grants a request.

decisions.choice: right and left: perhaps looking ahead to the cross
decisions.reason: When Jesus is crucified as king of the Jews, two rebels hang beside him, one on his right and one on his left (27:37-38). Matthew may want readers to see the irony, but he does not say so.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Give your word (B); Promise me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what she asks Jesus to say.

decisions.choice: when you rule as king
decisions.reason: Readable says what "your kingdom" means for her request.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν;
records.gloss: Answering now Jesus said, Not you know what you ask for; are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?
pieces: Jesus answered, "You do not realize what you are asking. The cup I am about to drink: are you able to drink it?"

L.22: But Jesus answered and said, "You do not know what you are asking for. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?"

R.22: Jesus answered, "You do not understand what you are asking for. I am going to drink a cup of suffering. Can you drink from that cup too?"

decisions.choice: the cup: the suffering God gives him to bear
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's judgment that the wicked must drink (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15; Psalm 75:8). In Gethsemane Jesus prays that this cup might pass from him (26:39).

decisions.choice: you: plural, the two brothers
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. Jesus turns from the mother to the sons, who answer him.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends with the cup
alternatives: adds: or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a saying about baptism here and in 20:23, which appears to come from Mark 10:38-39. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a cup of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα.
records.gloss: They say to him, We are able.
pieces: "We are able," they answered.

decisions.choice: we are able: a confident answer that they do not yet understand
alternatives: a true measure of their strength
decisions.reason: When Jesus is arrested, all the disciples leave him and run away (26:56).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου πίεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου.
records.gloss: He says to them, The indeed cup of me you will drink, but to sit on [the] right of me and on [the] left not is mine to give, but [to those] for whom it has been prepared by the Father of me.
pieces: He told them, "You will indeed drink {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} cup. But the places at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right and left are not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to hand out. They belong to those for whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has prepared them."

L.23: He says to them, "My cup you will indeed drink, but to sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right and at [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] left is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to give, but [it is for those] for whom it has been prepared by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father."

R.23: Jesus said to them, "Yes, you will drink from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} cup of suffering. But I am not the one who chooses who will sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left side. My Father has made those places ready, and they are for the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them ready for."

decisions.choice: you will drink my cup: they will share his suffering
decisions.reason: Jesus promises them suffering, not seats of honor. Herod Agrippa later put James to death with the sword (Acts 12:2).

decisions.choice: prepared by my Father: the Father decides who has those places
decisions.reason: Jesus leaves the places of honor to his Father, as he leaves the day of the end to him (24:36).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: I am not the one who chooses
decisions.reason: Readable says what giving the places means.

records.source: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν.
records.gloss: And having heard the ten were indignant about the two brothers.
pieces: The other ten were furious with the two brothers when they heard of this.

L.24: And when the ten heard [it], they became indignant about the two brothers.

R.24: The other ten followers heard about this, and they were angry with the two brothers.

decisions.choice: were indignant: angry at what they saw as wrong
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the chief priests in 21:15 and of the disciples in 26:8. The ten seem as eager for honor as the two.

decisions.choice: the other ten
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the ten are the rest of the Twelve.

records.heading: Great ones and servants

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And Jesus having called to [him] them said, You know that the rulers of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them and the great ones exercise authority over them.
pieces: Jesus called them together and said, "You know that among the Gentiles, rulers act as lords over their people, and the powerful wield their authority over them.

L.25: But Jesus called them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and said, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great ones exercise authority over them.

R.25: Jesus called them all together and said to them, "You know about the kings and rulers of other nations. They act like masters over the people they rule. Their important leaders use their power to control them.

decisions.choice: lord it over, exercise authority over: rule harshly, using power for themselves
decisions.reason: Both verbs are strengthened forms of the words for ruling and having authority. They suggest power used against those under it.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations of the world and their rulers
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of how kings and governors of the nations rule, as Rome ruled at that time.

decisions.choice: called them: all twelve
decisions.reason: Jesus calls the whole group, both the two and the angry ten.

decisions.choice: act like masters over
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: the speech runs on to 20:28
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer runs to the end of 20:28, so the quotation opens here and closes there.

records.source: οὐχ οὕτως ἔσται ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλ’ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος, καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος·
records.gloss: Not thus will it be among you; but whoever wishes among you great to become will be your servant, \v 27 and whoever wishes among you to be first will be your slave;
pieces: With you it must be different. If any of you wants to become great, that one must serve the rest of you.
And if any of you wants to be first, that one must be your slave.

L.26: It will not be so among you; but whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,
L.27: and whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave,

R.26: But it must not be like that with you. If anyone among you wants to be great, that person must serve the others.
R.27: If anyone wants to be first, that person must be your slave.

decisions.choice: will not be, will be: futures that work as commands
decisions.reason: As in the law ("you shall not"), the future tells what must be among Jesus's followers.

decisions.choice: servant: one who waits on others
decisions.reason: The word was used of those who served at table and did the work others needed.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by another, with no standing of his own
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than "servant". A slave belonged to a master. Jesus asks those who would be first to take the lowest place.

decisions.choice: will be
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "it is not so among you", as in Mark 10:43. The sense differs little. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: must
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of command.

decisions.choice: If any of you wants ..., that one must ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the relative clause into a condition, which reads more easily aloud.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where the word for slave stands against the word for servant in one saying: the step down from servant to slave is the point (m3).

records.source: ὥσπερ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
records.gloss: even as the Son of Man not came to be served but to serve and to give the life of him a ransom for many.
pieces: It is the same with the Son of Man. He did not come so that others would wait on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve them, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom for many."

L.28: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life [as] a ransom for many."

R.28: Be like the Son of Man. He did not come so that people would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve other people. He came to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom, a price paid to set many people free."

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to set a slave or captive free
decisions.reason: The word was used of money paid to free a slave or prisoner (Leviticus 25:51-52) and of a payment that saved a life that was forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12). Jesus gives his own life as that price.

decisions.choice: for many: in place of many, for a great number
decisions.reason: The preposition commonly means "in place of" or "in exchange for". "Many" sets the great number who are freed against the one who gives his life; it does not mean that others are left out (compare Isaiah 53:11-12).

decisions.choice: his death sets many free at the cost of his life
decisions.reason: Jesus's death is more than an example: it pays for the freedom of many. Matthew does not say to whom the ransom is paid. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of his blood poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins (26:28).

decisions.choice: the servant of Isaiah 53
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:10-12 tells of the servant whose life is made an offering for sin and who bears the sin of many. The word "ransom" is not in Isaiah 53, and some hear instead the language of God freeing his people from slavery (Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: It is the same with the Son of Man
alternatives: just as the Son of Man
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long sentence and makes the link to 20:26-27 a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Be like the Son of Man
alternatives: just as the Son of Man
decisions.reason: The words "just as" make the Son of Man the pattern for the disciples. Readable says so directly.

decisions.choice: a ransom, a price paid to set many people free
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a ransom is in a short added phrase.

records.source: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.
records.gloss: And going out them from Jericho followed him a crowd great.
pieces: A large crowd went along behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and the disciples left Jericho.

L.29: And as they were going out from Jericho, a large crowd followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.29: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were leaving the town of Jericho. A large crowd of people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Jericho: a town in the Jordan valley, the last stop before the climb to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jericho lay near the Jordan, about fifteen miles northeast of Jerusalem and far below it. Travelers from Galilee by the Jordan road went up to Jerusalem from there.

decisions.choice: they: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: The pronoun takes up Jesus and the Twelve from 20:17.

decisions.choice: he and the disciples (B); Jesus and his followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are.

records.heading: Two blind men by the Jericho road

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει, ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυίδ.
records.gloss: And behold two blind sitting beside the road, having heard that Jesus is passing by, cried out saying, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.
pieces: Beside the road sat two blind men. They heard that Jesus was passing, and they began to shout, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"

L.30: And look, two blind [men] sitting beside the road, hearing that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"

R.30: Two blind men were sitting beside the road. They heard that Jesus was going past, so they shouted, "Lord, Son of David, please have pity on us!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: a title for the promised king
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, the title names Jesus as the Messiah (1:1; 2 Samuel 7:12-16). The prophets said the blind would see when God came to save (Isaiah 35:5). Jesus is about to enter Jerusalem as the Son of David (21:9).

decisions.choice: two blind men
decisions.reason: As in 9:27 and 8:28, Matthew tells of two. Mark 10:46 names one of them, Bartimaeus.

decisions.choice: Lord, have mercy on us
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here: some lack "Lord", and some have "Jesus" in its place. The SBLGNT reads "Lord", as all agree in 20:31. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); absorbed (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: please have pity on us
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, Readable uses plain words for the cry.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν· οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυίδ.
records.gloss: And the crowd rebuked them that they should be silent; but they more cried out saying, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.
pieces: The crowd scolded them and told them to keep quiet, but they only shouted louder, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"

L.31: And the crowd rebuked them, that they should be silent; but they cried out all the more, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"

R.31: The people in the crowd told them off and said they must be quiet. But the men shouted even louder, "Lord, Son of David, please have pity on us!"

decisions.choice: rebuked: sternly told them to stop
decisions.reason: The disciples rebuked those who brought children in the same way (19:13). The crowd thinks the blind men are not worth Jesus's time.

decisions.choice: cried out all the more: louder and more urgently
decisions.reason: The word means more, or louder. The men will not be silenced.

decisions.choice: Lord, Son of David, please have pity on us
alternatives: Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David
decisions.reason: Readable gives the cry in the same words as in 20:30.

records.source: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;
records.gloss: And having stopped Jesus called them and said, What do you desire I should do to you?
pieces: Jesus stood still and called to them. "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked.

L.32: And Jesus stopped, called them, and said, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

R.32: Jesus stopped and called the men. He asked them, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do: an invitation to ask
alternatives: Jesus does not know their need
decisions.reason: Jesus asks them to say what they want, using nearly the same words he used to the mother of James and John (20:21).

decisions.choice: stopped: Jesus halts for them while the crowd moves on
decisions.reason: The crowd wanted them silent; Jesus stops the whole procession for them.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: They say to him, Lord, that might be opened the eyes of us.
pieces: "Lord," they replied, "we want our eyes to be opened."

L.33: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, [we want] our eyes to be opened."

R.33: They said, "Lord, we want to be able to see!"

decisions.choice: our eyes opened: to be given sight
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual one for giving sight to the blind (9:30).

decisions.choice: that: a request with the verb understood
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves "we want" unsaid; it answers the question in 20:32.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: we want
decisions.reason: English needs the verb that the Greek leaves understood. Literal brackets it.

records.source: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: Having been moved with compassion then Jesus touched the eyes of them, and immediately they received sight and they followed him.
pieces: Jesus felt deep pity for them and touched their eyes. At once they could see, and they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.34: And having compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they received sight and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.34: Jesus felt sorry for them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched their eyes. Right away they could see again. And they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: having compassion: moved deep within
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, the verb comes from the word for the inner organs, thought of as the seat of feeling. It is used in the Gospels almost only of Jesus (14:14; 15:32).

decisions.choice: eyes: a different word from the one in 20:33, with the same meaning
alternatives: a different part of the face
decisions.reason: Matthew uses a less common word for eyes here. It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: they followed him: they went with him, perhaps as disciples
alternatives: they only walked along with the crowd
decisions.reason: "Follow" is Matthew's word for discipleship (4:20, 22; 9:9), but it is also used of crowds who walk with Jesus (20:29). The healed men go with Jesus up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: they received sight
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "their eyes" after the verb. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: felt deep pity (B); felt sorry (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 9:36.
